tilted.label: Tilted (ball off the contacts, circuit open)

provenance.notes: Datasheet: Bailin (Beelee) SW-520 roll ball switch, model SW-520D, 2 pages (the copy linked from SunFounder's tilt-switch component page in its Vincent kit docs, read from the mirrors funduino.de/DL/SW-520D.pdf and 3v3.com.ua/data/files/SW-520D.PDF because tme.com serves a bot check). Page 2 drawing: body dia 5.2 mm, body length 11.5 mm, ball dia 3.5 +/-0.05 mm, lead dia 0.6 +/-0.05 mm, lead length 8 +/-1 mm, lead spacing 2.4 mm. The lead spacing is 1 pitch within 0.14 mm, so the part is rigid with the leads at [0,0] and [1,0]; the datasheet gives no bend allowance, so it is not a flex-2lead part. The two leads are not polarised. Page 1: contact rating 12 V, contact resistance below 10 ohm, insulation resistance above 10 MOhm, capacitance 5 pF. Distributor datasheet 100y.com.tw: 12 V, 5 mA, conduction time 2 ms, closed resistance below 10 ohm, open above 10 MOhm. The 5 mA limit is from that sheet only; the Bailin sheet gives no current limit. Conflicts: the manufacturer's web page gbeelee.com lists 1-6 V, 2 uA to 10 mA and closed resistance below 30 ohm. The lower voltage and current limits are the safer reading for a 3.3 V GPIO circuit. The ON/OFF angle is also inconsistent: Bailin's text says 10 degrees, its figure says 45 degrees, and the gbeelee page says 15 degrees. The sim therefore treats 'tilted' as a boolean with no angle. Behaviour: the switch is closed (ball resting on both contacts) when the leads point down and open when tilted far enough, which matches SunFounder's Tilt Switch page (upright = closed, tilted = open); 'tilted' = true means open. SunFounder's component list shows the SW-520D body ('Thermistor x1, Tilt Switch x1'). Its Fritzing diagram seats the leads in two adjacent rows of the same column.
